run.change_description: fix(utils/body,validator): normalize Content-Type media type for case-insensitive matching

summary.intent: Make parseBody() and validator() match supported Content-Type media types case-insensitively while leaving parameters such as multipart boundaries intact (issue #5060).
summary.issue_fit: Partial — every case-insensitivity requirement in issue #5060 is met, but the parseBody() rewrite regresses the formData()-then-parseBody() sequence that worked at the merge-base.
summary.coverage: All six changed files reviewed; focused body, buffer, validator and request tests passed at the head; the one candidate was verified in a fresh-context batch.
check_details: Reviewer ran vitest (project main, coverage off) on src/utils/body.test.ts, src/utils/buffer.test.ts, src/validator/validator.test.ts and src/request.test.ts at 5226d4165d48: 4 files passed, 144 tests passed, 1 skipped.

Reviewer ran a scratch probe (formData() then parseBody()) at the head: multipart returns a 500 TypeError and urlencoded returns a corrupted key; the same probe at the merge-base succeeds for both. Probe source: tmp.ZUVTdsdj4f/probe-source.ts.
No CI or other check evidence was supplied; the runtime-test suites for Deno, Bun, Workers and Lambda were unavailable.

findings.title: Reuse cached FormData in parseFormData
findings.trigger: A handler or middleware awaits c.req.formData() and then calls c.req.parseBody() on a multipart/form-data or application/x-www-form-urlencoded request.
findings.impact: parseFormData now calls arrayBuffer(), which re-serializes the cached FormData with a new boundary; parsing those bytes with the original Content-Type throws 'Failed to parse body as FormData.' for multipart and returns a corrupted key for urlencoded, where the merge-base returned the correct fields.
findings.change: In parseFormData, when the request is a HonoRequest and request.bodyCache.formData is already set, await it and convert that instead of calling arrayBuffer(), as src/validator/validator.ts does.
findings.source: Issue #5060 expected behavior and PR title: case-insensitive matching must not break existing parseBody() behavior; src/validator/validator.ts:115-116 shows the intended bodyCache.formData reuse.

requirements.evidence: src/utils/body.ts:106 lowercases the media type before matching; src/validator/validator.ts:24-26 regexes gain /i; src/utils/buffer.ts:113 lowercases only the part before ';'
body.test.ts, validator.test.ts and buffer.test.ts add mixed-case urlencoded, JSON and multipart cases; focused run passed
parseBody, validator and bufferToFormData match media types case-insensitively; see src/utils/body/parsebody-after-formdata for a regression in the same function
